name: Isotype Unit Chart
summary: Neurath-style picture statistics: countable pictogram rows where the anomaly is two carts that simply go missing.
look: Warm printed paper, ink rules and flat Gerd-Arntz-style pictograms in rows of ten. Teal and ink tokens; coral dashed ghosts mark the missing quantity. Mono FIG. captions like a 1930s atlas.

components.name: Pictogram token
components.role: one flat symbol = one fixed quantity, never scaled

components.name: Fractional cut
components.role: a sliced pictogram for partial values (8.2 carts)

components.name: Ghost token
components.role: dashed coral outline = what is missing, the anomaly itself

components.name: Figure rule + caption
components.role: ink rules and mono FIG. labels that make it feel printed

components.name: Legend key
components.role: icon = value line, always on screen so the count is honest

components.name: Isotype arrow
components.role: chunky flat arrow for the collapse into the Acme mark

motion.name: Token stamp
motion.how: each pictogram scales 1.15 → 1 with a 2-frame opacity pop, stagger 0.0625 s (1/16 at 120 BPM), back.out(2)

motion.name: Collapse-to-symbol
motion.how: rows translate to the arrow with power3.in 0.5 s (one beat), mark appears on the drop with a 3-frame white flash

motion.name: Ghost reveal
motion.how: missing carts fade 0 → 1 over 0.25 s on snare hits (beats 2 and 4), stroke-dashoffset crawls 6 px per beat

story: Hook stamps 38 dashboard tokens and one coral one nobody noticed. On the drop they collapse through an Isotype arrow into the Acme mark. Proof: a row of 10 checkout carts before 09:42 and 8.2 after deploy #2231, the missing ones dashed in coral, then Roll back. CTA: seven builder figures ship, one mark watches — Start free.
adapt: Pick one countable unit your users care about (orders, builds, tickets, seats) and draw it as a flat 2-colour pictogram; let the anomaly be tokens that go missing or turn coral.

references.note: Neurath/Arntz principle: more quantity = more identical symbols, not bigger ones

fit.risk: Pictograms can read as childish if the grid, rules and mono captions are not kept strict and printed-looking.
